video.title: The Most Hands-Off Side Hustle Anyone Can Copy

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Peter Askew (askew.org, Deep South Ventures), who has spent 20 years building small online businesses around exact-match domains, mostly bought patiently at expired-domain auctions. He started by buying neglected but well-ranked mom-and-pop websites and adding AdSense (Travel Envoy cost $10k, earned $1-2k/month and paid back in six months), then bought DudeRanch.com for about $18k and turned it into a flat-fee advertising directory (about 60 advertisers, a little over $50k a year from about an hour a month). He also runs RanchWork, a hand-curated ranch job board ($99+ per posting, 1.3M visits a year), and Vidalia onions sold direct to consumers with a partner farm (100,000 lb shipped this year, using Shopify and ShipStation). Key lessons: let a great domain's type-in traffic and authority be the marketing channel, keep your day job until side projects out-earn it, give partners no-risk offers, and be patient.

speakers.name: Peter Askew
speakers.description: Domain investor and builder (askew.org, Deep South Ventures); runs DudeRanch.com, RanchWork and a Vidalia onion DTC business with A&M Farms

ideas.name: Exact-match industry directory (DudeRanch.com)
ideas.one_liner: Buy a descriptive expired .com for a high-ticket niche and sell flat-fee listings to the businesses in that industry.
ideas.business_model: Flat yearly listing fee paid by advertisers; no commission on bookings
ideas.customer: Dude/guest ranch owners (advertisers); families searching for ranch vacations (users)
ideas.problem: Ranches need bookings for $10k-30k family vacations; searchers want a trusted overview with photos and video
ideas.offer: Listing on DudeRanch.com (and GuestRanches.com) with photos, video and info, driving leads directly to ranches

pricing.notes: He describes it both as a flat yearly fee and as a one-time fee; no cut of conversions.

acquisition_channels.details: Signed first advertisers at the dude ranch industry's annual conference held at a ranch.

quote.text: they have a yearly conference every year they hold it at a dude ranch typically
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

acquisition_channels.details: Exact-match domain plus SEO; type-in traffic of 30-50 visits a day from day one; AI assistants now also cite it.

quote.text: When I got Dude Ranch, right out of the gate, I was getting 30 to 50 visits a day from people typing in Dude Ranch
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

acquisition_channels.details: Partnered with competitor GuestRanches.com so cancelling both would lose ranches ~50% of traffic; later bought him out.

ideas.delivery: WordPress site; a contractor fixes PHP/plugin issues for a couple hundred dollars a year.
unit_economics_claims: ~60 advertisers at $575; a little over $50k a year
About an hour a month of work
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated (advertisers came after the first conference)

acquisition.how: SEO/type-in traffic is automatic; advertiser sign-ups via self-serve, though early sales were in person. UK PECR permits cold email only to limited companies; many small venues are sole traders.

onboarding.how: Self-serve listing purchase and profile forms.

delivery.how: Static directory serving leads; agents could maintain listings and content.

support.how: Agents can handle listing edits; site breakages need a developer.

uk_applicability.notes: Model works for UK niches (e.g. glamping, farm stays) if a strong exact-match domain is obtainable; dude ranches themselves are US-specific.

risks: Depends on owning a scarce premium domain

pricing.notes: Just raised prices and added a diamond level; refunds sketchy listings.

acquisition_channels.details: SEO-optimised job board architecture on a fast server; 1.3M visits a year.

quote.text: We get 1.3 million visits a year to this site

Word of mouth and repeat buyers each hiring season.

ideas.delivery: Peter hand-reviews every listing and posts jobs daily to show the board is alive.
unit_economics_claims: Started as a 75/25 revenue split with the domain owner; bought out for ~$10k after ~6 years

acquisition.how: SEO and repeat employers bring listings inbound.

delivery.how: Agents could pre-screen listings and cross-post; he hand-curates today.

ideas.name: Direct-to-consumer Vidalia onions with a partner farm
ideas.one_liner: Use a premium domain to sell a regional boutique crop direct to consumers while the farm handles packing and shipping.
ideas.business_model: DTC product sales split with partner farm at year-end
ideas.customer: Consumers nationwide wanting Georgia Vidalia sweet onions
ideas.problem: Farmers sell through distributors and chains and hate DTC; consumers can't easily buy Vidalias online
ideas.offer: Online orders of Vidalia onions packed and shipped by UPS from A&M Farms with climate-controlled storage for summer shipping

pricing.notes: Not the cheapest option; revenue not disclosed, only volume.

acquisition_channels.details: Exact-match domain type-in and search traffic; started with an email-signup landing page to test demand.
30-second phone videos (tractor, holding an onion, packing shed) with link in bio.
Approached the Vidalia committee, toured farms; third farmer (Aries) agreed to a no-risk handshake deal.

ideas.delivery: Farm crew packs in the packing shed; Peter runs website, marketing, sales, social and customer support.
unit_economics_claims: 100,000 lb shipped this year, a record
onions.com bought for $14,800 for email/branding; ~50 type-in visits/day

acquisition.how: SEO, type-in and social ads can be largely automated.

delivery.how: Growing, grading and packing onions is physical (done by partner).

support.how: He still does support himself and it 'about broke my brain'; agents could handle most with ShipStation tracking.

uk_applicability.notes: Model of marketing a protected regional product (e.g. Jersey Royals, Yorkshire rhubarb) online for a farm works; Vidalia itself is US-only. Trademarked/protected names need permission.

tactics.name: Buy under-monetised ranking websites
steps: Google high-CPC terms (e.g. tourism destinations)
Find dated sites ranking top 3 with no ads
Ask owners for analytics
Estimate AdSense income at 1-3% CTR x CPC x 70%
Offer roughly a 6-9 month payback price (e.g. $10k)
Secure the domain first, then migrate content and add ads/affiliates

quote.text: I got to get control of this domain because if I control the domain, I control the whole site
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: Validate an expired domain before bidding
steps: Check search volume for the term and intent (e.g. 'dude ranch vacation' vs band album)
Check state/long-tail variants
Estimate customer ticket size and their margin
Check domain age and GoDaddy traffic stats for type-in traffic
Bid patiently; wait for the right name rather than building ideas first

quote.text: I wanted search volume. I want to fish where the fish are
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: Corner a niche by partnering with the competitor
steps: Notice advertisers cancel one directory but keep the other
Partner with the competing directory
Cancelling both would cost them ~50% of traffic, reducing churn
Eventually buy the partner out

quote.text: if they cancel both of us, they're going to lose about 50% of their traffic
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: No-risk partner offers
steps: Offer to do all the online work for free
Domain owner keeps the domain and points nameservers to you (RanchWork 75/25 split)
Farm keeps fulfilment; you only get paid if you generate sales
Keep talking to people until you find the one who 'just gets it'

quote.text: I'll build you a website for free you have to pay me a penny and then let's just see if we can ship some onions
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: Test demand with a landing page
steps: Put up a simple page with email signup ('interested in having Vidalias delivered?')
Watch sign-ups
Then visit the industry body and farms to find a fulfilment partner
Get the trademark holder's blessing

tactics.name: Run a job board that looks alive
steps: Buy an off-the-shelf WordPress job board theme (~$60) and tune it for SEO on a fast server
Seed listings from existing advertisers and ranch websites
Post jobs every day to signal activity
Hand-curate each listing within 24 hours; refund sketchy ones
Don't force account creation; cross-post to email and Facebook group
Tier pricing by listing duration; offer a free tier for ranches in trouble

quote.text: I like consistency on my job board to alert folks that this thing is alive and kicking
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: Cheap 30-second phone video ads for DTC
steps: Film three clips (tractor, product in hand, packing shed)
Write a quick script, aim for ~30 seconds
Edit in CapCut, track with Facebook pixel
Use to test whether a boutique product sells

tactics.name: Proactive lost-parcel handling
steps: Track all orders in ShipStation
Detect lost boxes before the customer notices
Claim with UPS or ship a make-good immediately

quote.text: I'd like to find out that the box has been lost before the customer realizes that the box has been lost
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

tactics.name: Use a premium domain for credibility email
steps: Give partners and staff emails on a category-killer domain (e.g. @onions.com via Fastmail)
Use the simpler domain to redirect customers who misspell the brand

warnings.warning: Don't quit your job to go all in on a side project; pressure kills creative ideas.

quote.text: some online builders are under the impression that they need to quit their day job
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

warnings.warning: Regional product names can be trademarked by law (Vidalia); get the industry's blessing.

quote.text: it's a trademark term by the state law. I almost needed their blessing to use it
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

warnings.warning: Customer support at volume overwhelms a solo operator; delegate.

quote.text: I'm still doing customer support, Chris, and it about broke my brain this year
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

warnings.warning: Handshake partnership deals carry risk, though it worked for him.
Sites get burnt down, de-indexed or fail to earn; expect many failures over years.
If you don't control the domain, a seller can back out of a site deal.

lessons.lesson: Keep your day job until the side project out-earns it (the wing walker's code).

quote.text: You never let go of one railing until you have control of the other railing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Let a great descriptive domain be the marketing channel: type-in traffic and instant trust.

quote.text: With a an exact match descriptive.com generic exact match is wildly powerful
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Build from assets that inspire you (domains, channels) rather than from ideas first.

quote.text: When I shifted my perspective to build and be inspired by domains, things started working
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Information arbitrage: owners often don't know what their traffic is worth.
Partners make projects work; offer them no-brainer, no-risk deals.

quote.text: If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go together
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Sales is finding the person who 'just gets it', not convincing everyone.
Suppliers who hate DTC are opportunities: you become their distribution and they capture higher margin.
Directories still work in the AI era when they offer trusted photos, video and info; AI tools even recommend them.

quote.text: AI is helping as well because AI is making suggestions on here are some ranches, but hey, here's dude ranch.com
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Build a failure callous: iterate through failures until a path emerges (5 years from start to DudeRanch).

quote.text: You keep doing it enough you keep failing enough that callous is going to form
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Premium domains come up at reasonable prices once in a lifetime; buy when available.

quote.text: there's one time in our lifetime that domain's going to be for sale
quote.speaker: Peter Askew

lessons.lesson: Mix seasonal and year-round projects to spread attention across the year.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific prices, revenue, traffic and domain costs across several projects; Vidalia revenue not disclosed and some figures are approximate.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsor read for beehiiv; Chris promotes TK Owners.
